title: He knew the miracle was minutes away…
paragraphs:
He knew the miracle was minutes away…
and still—He broke down and cried.

Why would God weep…
when He already planned the ending?

Why feel grief…
when resurrection was already in His mouth?

because what looks like weakness
is actually a window into the heart of God.

Jesus stood in front of a tomb…
but the real burial wasn’t just Lazarus.

Because what you see in that scene
is not just death.
It’s what sin has done to us.

The silence of a body that once laughed.
The echo of love that now has nowhere to land.
The unbearable finality of goodbye.
And here’s the part that hits deep—

Romans 5:12 says,
“Therefore, just as sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because all sinned.”
Death is not just an event.

And every grave…
is a receipt.

Not because He was powerless—
but because He was looking at what sin had done to the people He loved.

The relationship you quietly ruined.
The purity you traded for a moment.
The lie you justified… then repeated… then became.

James 1:15 says,
“Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death.”

Romans 3:23 says,
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
So when Jesus stood there, tears in His eyes…

Your hidden shame.
Your quiet guilt.
Your carefully managed image that hides a breaking soul.
We’d distance ourselves from broken things.

John 11:33 says,
“He was deeply moved in His spirit and greatly troubled.”
That phrase “deeply moved” in the original language carries the idea of a groaning… even a kind of righteous anger.

1 Corinthians 15:26 says,
“The last enemy to be destroyed is death.”
He was confronting the destruction of everything good.

Love interrupted.
Life stolen.
Hope buried.
He knew He was about to reverse it.
But He still chose to feel it.

He didn’t skip the pain…
just because He had the power.
Some of you have been wondering—

Psalm 34:18 says,
“The Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.”
He’s not waiting for you to be okay.
He meets you while you’re not.
But here’s where the story shifts.
And He shouted into the impossible:

Because every one of us
is spiritually Lazarus.

Ephesians 2:1 says,
“And you were dead in the trespasses and sins.”

Dead means no response.
No life.
No ability to save yourself.

Religion can’t fix that.
Good works can’t revive that.
Self-improvement can’t resurrect that.
And here’s the Gospel—clear and unfiltered:

Your sin leads to death.
You cannot escape it on your own.

But Jesus Christ—
the Son of God—
stepped into our death.

2 Corinthians 5:21 says,
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
He didn’t just cry at a grave.

On the cross, He carried your sin.
Your shame.
Your secret life.
Your worst moment.
He didn’t just call someone else out of the grave.

1 Corinthians 15:55 says,
“O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?”
So now the question is not—
Why are you still living like the grave has the final word?

Why are you still hiding in shame
when grace is calling your name?

Why are you still bound
when the stone has already been rolled away?
Turn from the sin you’ve been protecting.

1 John 1:9 says,
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
He’s not waiting to condemn you.
To call you out of the grave.
But as a command filled with life:

Come out of hiding.
Come out of addiction.
Come out of pride.
Come out of shame.
Because the same Jesus who wept over death…
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.
